articles.excerpt: Candy was recalled in 13 states, including Ohio and Indiana, due to an undeclared allergen.
articles.content:

CINCINNATI (WKRC) - Candy was recalled in 13 states, including Ohio and Indiana, due to an undeclared allergen.

According to a recall report from the Food and Drug Administration, bags of "Chocolately Eyeballs" sold under the Crystal Temptations brand at Marshalls, TJ Maxx, Homegoods, and Sierra Trading Post were recalled because their packaging did not declare the presence of milk in the product.

The candies were recalled in Arizona, Texas, Virginia, Georgia, Massachusetts, North Carolina, Indiana, Nevada, California, New Jersey, Connecticut, Ohio, and Wyoming.

The products affected by the recall were:

Customers were advised to "destroy the product" and the report advised that refunds would not be available at the point of sale. Instead, customers were told to contact Crystal Temptations with proof of purchase for a refund.

articles.title: I Love to Read: World’s top creator and bestselling author release high-stakes thriller
articles.excerpt: MrBeast and James Patterson launch their global thriller 'The Most Dangerous Games' today, featuring a high-stakes $1 billion contest.
articles.content:
INDIANAPOLIS (WISH) — YouTube creator MrBeast and bestselling author James Patterson have teamed up for a new thriller that combines high-stakes competition with a fight for humanity’s survival.

“The Most Dangerous Games” launches globally Sept. 1, 2026.

The novel follows 100 contestants competing in a secretive competition with a $1 billion prize. As the games unfold, the stakes go beyond winning, with the fate of humanity tied to the outcome.

The book brings together the world of MrBeast, whose real name is Jimmy Donaldson, and Patterson’s decades of experience writing bestselling thrillers.

Donaldson is known for large-scale challenges, elaborate competitions and philanthropy campaigns. He also founded Beast Industries and operates one of the most-subscribed individual channels on YouTube.

Patterson is the author of hundreds of books and has received numerous honors, including an Edgar Award, 10 Emmy Awards, the Literarian Award and the National Humanities Medal.

The two discussed the collaboration during a virtual event Aug. 13, highlighting how Donaldson’s experience with competition and entertainment influenced the story while Patterson brought his thriller-writing expertise to the project.

HarperCollins acquired the rights to the book and is distributing it worldwide.

“The Most Dangerous Games” is available in standard, deluxe limited and digital editions through major retailers.More information can be found here.

articles.title: Under Trump, the IRS’ audit revenue falls in predictable and damaging ways
articles.excerpt: Following sweeping cuts, the tax agency brought in 35% less last year than the year before, and there’s no great mystery as to why.
articles.content:
Donald Trump’s second term has been a difficult one for the IRS. The tax agency has struggled with resignations, DOGE-imposed disruptions and the abandonment of a much-needed modernization initiative.

Complicating matters, there’s been a revolving door at the IRS administrator’s office. In the first seven months of Trump’s second term, seven different people led the agency. The eighth was Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who already had another important full-time job. Since March, no one has served as IRS commissioner, although the White House tapped Frank Bisignano to serve as the agency’s chief executive officer (an office that’s never existed before), despite the fact that he also has a full-time job running the Social Security Administration.

With all of this tumult, it’s tempting to ask how the IRS can be expected to fulfill its core functions. The answer to that question is that it’s not completing some of its core functions. The New York Times reported:

articles.title: Stephanie Thomas unsure if report of federal elections probe is true
articles.excerpt: Secretary of the State Stephanie Thomas said she does not know if CT under investigation by the Trump administration for possible voter fraud.
articles.content:

Secretary of the State Stephanie Thomas called a noon press conference Tuesday to share that she does not know if Connecticut is one of nine states under investigation by the Trump administration for possible voter fraud, as reported Monday by CNN, nor has she done anything to find out.

Quoting an internal document, CNN reported that an investigative arm of the Department of Homeland Security planned a “coordinated criminal voter fraud surge initiative to pursue investigative leads, conduct field interviews, and support timely prosecutorial review.”

Thomas said she called the press conference to reassure the voting public and combat misinformation, albeit with no information other than an indication in the CNN report that the Homeland Security Investigations office of DHS was interested in finding noncitizens on the voter rolls.

Has your office reached out to DHS?

“We have not,” Thomas replied.

Why not?

“Honestly, I haven’t had time yet this morning, and I assume they will reach out to us,” Thomas replied. “I’m also waiting to see if there’s any more information that comes in about whether or not this is actually happening, or just one media report.”

In an unsigned statement Tuesday to the Connecticut Mirror, a DHS spokesperson would not confirm the investigation that CNN said was to be launched Tuesday, but broadly acknowledged that finding noncitizens on the voter rolls was a priority:

“While ICE Homeland Security Investigations is not able to comment on any active investigations, HSI is actively rooting out and investigating election fraud wherever it can be found. We have repeatedly demonstrated that illegal aliens can and do vote in our elections. Under President Trump, HSI is committed to restoring integrity to our election systems and ensuring that American citizens and only American citizens are electing American leaders.”

The agency says it has evidence that as many as 24,000 foreign citizens have registered to vote, but it provided details of only four persons who have been prosecuted.

“DHS is laser focused on prosecuting and removing aliens who vote and preventing the dilution of the votes of U.S. citizens, the DHS spokesperson said. “Our message to aliens who vote in American elections is clear: we will find you, arrest you, and you will face the consequences — including criminal charges and deportation.”

Thomas said no local registrar of voters has reported being approached by federal investigators about any voter on their rolls.

“Whether the news report is true or not, what I am addressing to Connecticut voters is that we will have an election, that there are many people, many agencies working to make sure that it is a secure election on many fronts,” Thomas said. “And that if something should happen, we have the people and the tools to address it.”

One person recently detained by ICE in West Hartford was found to be a registered voter, but it was unclear if that was the result of fraud or an error at the Department of Motor Vehicles. The DMV automatically takes an initial step to register people who are getting licenses after asking them to attest they are a citizen. Local officials make the final determination.

A review by the secretary of the state’s office found that the man never had voted, and his name already has been stricken from the voters after he failed to respond to an annual canvass.

“One of the most important steps that happen all year are voter roll maintenance. Obviously, our registrars are following the statutes,” Thomas said. “They’re doing the annual canvass. They are getting reports about potential duplicate voters, people who may have moved out of state.”

Rep. Gale Mastrofrancesco, R-Wolcott, the ranking Republican on the committee that oversees election bills, said a federal investigation would be welcome.

“If there is nothing to find, then an independent investigation will confirm that,” she said in a statement. “If there are problems, Connecticut voters deserve to know about them and deserve to know that those responsible will be held accountable.”

Mark PazniokasCapitol Bureau Chief

Mark is the Capitol Bureau Chief and a co-founder of CT Mirror. He is a frequent contributor to WNPR, a former state politics writer for The Hartford Courant and Journal Inquirer, and contributor for The New York Times.

articles.title: Cyrus Allen provides Chiefs fans a glimpse into the respect Patrick Mahomes demands
articles.excerpt: The Kansas City Chiefs are uber-excited about Cyrus Allen, who, in turn, pointed out how exciting it is to work alongside Super Bowl MVP Patrick Mahomes.
articles.content:
There has been an undeniable level of disrespect swirling around the Kansas City Chiefs and Patrick Mahomes after a rough 2025 season. It's as if one year of failure gave permission for league pundits and fans to get every wrong take off their chest when it comes to Mahomes and KC. Underrating Mahomes is a dangerous decision, one that fellow players clearly don't make the mistake of doing.

Fifth-round rookie and training camp darling, Cyrus Allen is the latest example of how Mahomes has continued to demand respect and inspire his teammates despite the quarterback's lessened numbers over the last three regular seasons.

In last year's injury-shortened season, Mahomes finished with 3,587 passing yards and 22 passing touchdowns. These are good numbers in a full season for nearly half the league; only by the lofty standards the three-time Super Bowl MVP has established would this be an invitation to cast doubt and rank less accomplished players ahead of him.

Gabriela Hernandez of KWCH10 News provided a glimpse of the respect Mahomes still garners. "I'm still lookin' at Pat like, 'Damn, this Patrick Mahomes I'm around...," Allen said postgame after a preseason loss. This points to the undeniable legend who has a young player starstruck. It serves as a reminder of who Mahomes is, no matter the recent numbers.

Kansas City's fifth-round rookie and training camp darling was starstruck playing alongside the three-time Super Bowl MVP

There is still no one in the league who can compare their resume to that of Mahomes and have a fair argument. There is already a valid argument to be made that the signal-caller is only behind Tom Brady when having the GOAT conversation.

It is important to remember that recent seasons have seen numbers decline based not on ability, but on the cast around the quarterback as well as playcalling. The lack of investment in the receiver room since Tyreek Hill left exposes just how much Kansas City has grown to rely on Mahomes. It seems the Chiefs have simply believed that anything close to a capable offensive line will be more than enough to provide the Chiefs a chance to make a Super Bowl run.

This cannot be denied when you consider the past two groups of receivers that Mahomes has taken to a Super Bowl. In fact, the majority of the Chiefs' wide receiver room during the 2023 season is now out of the league. Patrick Mahomes dragged those dudes to a Super Bowl victory.

articles.title: Is MrBeast and James Patterson’s Novel Collaboration Headed for a Disastrous Debut?
articles.excerpt: MrBeast and James Patterson's snew novel collaboration, The Most Dangerous Games, has been tracking poorly in presales, according to a report.
articles.content:
As of last week, preorders for 'The Most Dangerous Games' were reportedly "numbering in the four digits." But sources insist the authors are on track.

Could MrBeast and James Patterson have a dud on their hands?

According to Semafor, the pair’s new novel collaboration, titled The Most Dangerous Games, has been tracking poorly in presales.

Citing anonymous sources “close to the project,” Semafor reported that the thriller is “on track to be a historic bomb.” As of last week, preorders were “numbering in the four digits … a tiny fraction of what the publisher will need to justify Patterson’s and YouTuber Jimmy Donaldson’s [aka MrBeast] hefty fees.” As of Monday, the book was at No. 18 on Amazon’s new releases list.

However, another knowledgeable source told The Hollywood Reporter that the number of preorders is not unusual, particularly for a genre novel, and that what really matters is first-week sales. They also pointed out that the book is currently at No. 1 on the mystery novels list.

The Hollywood Reporter has reached out to reps for book publisher HarperCollins for comment.

According to the book’s webpage, the logline is: “A thousand strangers receive the invitation. One hundred make the cut. An unprecedented competition from MrBeast, the world’s #1 creator with more than a billion followers, and James Patterson, the world’s #1 bestselling author, where the stakes couldn’t be higher.

“The Games begin in Antarctica, where one wrong step “on the ice kills you, and they never let up: Shark water off a remote Chilean island, desert heat that cooks you where you stand, storm-battered peaks, and caves so black you cannot find your own hand. No rescue. No second chances. A billion dollars to whoever is still standing.

“Then the terrain stops being the thing that can kill you, and the other players start. Alliances turn into ambushes. Trust becomes the sharpest weapon. And somewhere above it all, a hidden voice is watching every move, testing, deciding who deserves to survive.”

Donaldson and Patterson have been promoting the book on social media, including in a YouTube short titled “Read My Book, You Could Win $1,000,000.” Donaldson, who has 515 million subscribers on YouTube, is known for giving away money to his followers for taking part in (and successfully completing) various outlandish stunts.
